mutants.note: qualifyingWeek is a Sunday, so +6 is a Saturday and +7 the next Sunday. Every RATES boundary is 6 April and rateAt falls back to RATES[0] before the first one; the only later boundary (2026-04-06) is a Monday, so no Saturday/Sunday pair straddles a rate change and the LEL looked up is identical. Becomes live if an earlier year (2024/25, 6 April 2024 a Saturday) is added.

Off by one day at the 26-week boundary (start on the Monday 25 weeks before the qualifying week). Not pinned: the current formula itself may be up to 6 days too strict (real_defects[1]); a test fixing the boundary should come with that decision.
No test priced SMP weeks across an April uprating; added 'each SMP week takes the standard rate in force on its own date'.

real_defects.issue: Due dates before 6 April 2025 were priced with the 2025/26 standard rate (a 2024-09-01 due date paid 2024/25 weeks at £187.18, not the 2024/25 rate) and tested against the 2025/26 LEL, with no warning (only the future edge had one). Reproduced with compute(); fixed with a 'before 6 April 2025' finding and a failing-first test.

Possible: eligibility() counts whole 7-day blocks back from the end of the qualifying week, so a parent must have started by the Sunday 25 weeks before the qualifying week. HMRC's Statutory Payments Manual (SPM250800, via search summary) says a week counts if any work was done in it, and ERA 1996 s.212(1) counts a week employed in part, which would allow a start any day up to that Saturday (6 days later). Not fixed: gov.uk and legislation.gov.uk were unreachable from this session (proxy 403 / DNS), so the rule could not be confirmed from the primary text. Fix if confirmed: lengthOk = emp <= qualifyingWeek - 169 (and employedWeeks computed from sundayOnOrBefore(emp)); then pin the boundary with a test, which also guards mutant at line 69.

certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured
